content:
Hi dear friend,

I, I have a project closed and locked, could some give some advice?

I spent some time to have this project with the help of different AI, and I want it to be mathlib pr.

maybe it contains too many aspects, so if I make it as small aspect as I can, could it be unlocked and I can continue?

Another problem of this is on Axioms. I know the rules of new Axioms. But I have to say without some Axioms, I can not introduce the new whole contents.

The only way, seems to be small and only one theorem or one lemma?

Note the advice about AI PRs on the community website [here] (https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/index.html#use-of-ai) and in particular the comment that mathlib has high code quality standards and that AI-written code usually fails to meet that bar by a wide margin. Thus I think it would not be welcome to have AI-generated PRs written by someone who is not already a Lean expert.

Yes, Thank you!

And I want to rewrite the code and submit the minimum number of lemma and theory, just 1+1 case.

In this way, could my project be open?

Or I just resubmit the new project?

Why are you not putting up any links? What is the "project" you're referring to, do you mean a PR that is closed with comments locked? You can put your GitHub account in your Zulip profile, by the way.
They mean #37337, and I believe this is the second thread they've opened about it.
I think the previous thread might have been deleted.

It might be attempting to formalize some theory from https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-981-97-8727-2 which I have never heard of (looks like something fuzzy mathematics); apparently there is some Chinese association dedicated to it.

Interesting the author (or the AI) uses Gray sometimes (nothing to do with Gray code) and Grey sometimes

Another PR #35976 by the same author is still open.

Junyan Xu said:

Another PR #35976 by the same author is still open.

I haven't gone through all of this but isn't this just a probability space by another name?
Uncertainty.Theory.Book.pdf is the reference (5th ed.). This is the difference according to the author (appendix B.3):

Uncertainty Theory is some kind new theory to discuss the uncertainty, it with the same position(level) to Probability according to Prof. Baoding LIU in book Uncertainty Theory (it has edition 1 to 5th) , and its the main references for PR #35976, and from https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-662-44354-5 both Fourth and Fifth edition.

But Grey Theory is different. Grey Theory is claimed to be another kind theory to discuss the uncertainty. It's more like to be used in engineering areas.

It's base some like Fuzzy theory to some degree, but totally different.

This is the book https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-981-97-8727-2 , Grey Systems Analysis: Methods, Models and Applications》(Second Edition) , I take it as the main references for PR #37337

For the last 40 years, researches have developed many theories on Grey System. But NOT with LEAN. My objective is to find a feasible way to formalize the Grey theories.

The basis of Grey Theory is some Axioms, some like man-defined not completely generated the traditional math theories.

Unfortunately, Lean does not accept new Axioms.

This is my biggest problem to be resolved, for me.

Even with the help of AI, I still spent more than 3 months to do the LEAN proof of PR #37337 , Because AI always gave me the wrong way, totally wrong many times. I have to check all the time, and with my ideas to direct AI to help me to do the LEAN proof.

In my original idea, I want to recover all the definitions, axioms, theories of Grey Theories in LEAN, But IT IS IMPOSSIBLE currently.

So I choose some to realize in LEAN. But still, I found some theories are constraint in GREY THEORY Concepts. That is, not in Mathematical proof way.

That is the main reason, I want to open the 37337.
Thank you.
I think there is a misunderstanding here: formalizing in Lean is not the same as merging into Mathlib. I would say the latter is a lot harder and is not always a suitable goal for every project.

Thank you!

Yes, This is also the reason I want to merge. As Grey Theory NEEDS LEAN for the future in AI era.
(deleted)

I think you should make your own repository developing Grey theory, just like the physics people have their own Lean repository and the computer science people have their own Lean repository. I am not sure that this topic is suitable for mathlib, but that doesn't stop you from using Lean!

Yeah probably no current mathlib reviewer is familiar with these theories. And I'm not sure the theories are mainstream enough that a lot of people would want them in mathlib.

Looking at the PR, I don't see the two axioms general_gray_add_nonneg and general_gray_add_le_one actually used anywhere. If they are to be used, can't you just make them hypotheses just like you use BookAxiomSet as a typeclass assumption in #35976?

Thank you !

This is because the submitted edition are the abridged version.

And thank you for your advice, I will try BookAxiomSet as a typeclass assumption in #35976. Excellent!

LEAN is the base in the future, at least in my mind.

This is direct reason for Grey Theory and Uncertainty Theory to be LEANed in Mathlib.

Maybe just some basic concepts and theories as initial , and more theories are to be left for the future resolve.

Hi all, thanks again for the guidance.

And frankly speaking, AI, LLM can not generate the RIGHT GREY codes in LEAN.

Actually, I guided the LLM and corrected the codes myself and finally I had this version.
